sources.entry: ralph-orchestrator by mikeyobrien - Ralph Orchestrator implements the simple but effective "Ralph Wiggum" technique for autonomous task completion, continuously running an AI agent against a prompt file until the task is marked as complete or limits are reached. This implementation provides a robust, well-tested, and feature-complete orchestration system for AI-driven development. Also cited in th

summary.one_liner: A hat-based orchestration framework that runs AI coding agents in a loop against a prompt until the task is complete or limits are hit (the "Ralph Wiggum" technique).
summary.what_it_does: Ralph repeatedly runs an AI coding assistant CLI until it outputs a LOOP_COMPLETE marker or reaches an iteration limit. Work is organized into "hats," specialized personas that coordinate through events. Backpressure gates (tests, lint, typecheck) are described as rejecting incomplete work. It includes persistent memories and runtime task tracking, plus a planning command (ralph plan) that creates requirements, design, and implementation-plan files under .ralph/specs/. It supports multiple backends (Claude Code, Kiro, Gemini CLI, Codex, Forge, Amp, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Roo, OMP) and five builtin hat presets. Optional features include an alpha web dashboard (ralph web), an MCP server mode over stdio, and Telegram-based human-in-the-loop interaction where agents can ask questions and humans can send guidance mid-loop.
use_cases: Autonomously completing coding tasks with an AI agent in a loop
Planning a feature into specs before implementation
Adding input validation or small changes via a single prompt
Monitoring orchestration loops in a web dashboard
Exposing agent loop control to MCP-compatible clients
Getting human answers or guidance from Telegram during an agent run
how_to_run: ralph plan "Add user authentication with JWT"
notable: Hat system: specialized personas coordinating through events
Backpressure gates that reject work failing tests, lint, or typecheck
Supports many AI coding CLI backends behind one loop
Telegram human-in-the-loop with reply-to and @loop-id routing for parallel loops
MCP server mode scoped to one workspace root per instance
caveats: Web dashboard is in Alpha with expected rough edges and breaking changes
Requires an external AI coding assistant CLI to be installed; needs Rust toolchain and Node.js for the dashboard
Homebrew is not currently published from the automated release flow
